means: Colour fringing at high-contrast edges - a red or cyan halo where the lens failed to bring all wavelengths to focus on the same plane.
does: Almost nothing as a prompt tag. The effect lives at the scale of one or two pixels on an edge, below anything a diffusion sampler steers reliably, so asking for it mostly re-rolls the frame. It IS available exactly and for free in post: short.py fx aberr is rgbashift=rh=4:bh=-4:rv=-2:bv=2, shifting red four pixels one way and blue four the other. Use that. One hazard - aberr shifts channels, the grade tints, and hot pushes saturation; stacked they compounded into solid magenta across a third of a film, which is why the day-for-night grade now holds saturation down at 0.72 to leave headroom.
reach_for_it: for damage, glitch, a broken reality layer, a cheap lens - and reach for the fx, not the tag
used_in: the aberr option of studio/cards/shot_fx.json ('chromatic aberration, color fringing'); short.py fx_chain() aberr branch; studio/cards/story_reality_layer.json
